result.summary: Validates the bucket array deserialized from `fee_estimates.dat` (or `block_policy_estimates.dat`) upon loading. Specifically, it rejects fee estimate data if the first bucket is not positive, if bucket values do not strictly increase, or if the final bucket is not infinite.
result.problem: When loading fee estimation history from disk, malformed or corrupted bucket lists lacking an infinite terminating bucket can cause subsequent feerate lookups to read past the end of the bucket map.
evidence: Author description: 'A block_policy_estimates.dat whose bucket list lacks the infinite last bucket makes a later feerate lookup read past the end of the bucket map.'

Author commit message: 'The estimator relies on the last bucket being infinite, so that every feerate finds a bucket. I reject a list whose first bucket is not positive, that does not strictly increase, or that does not end with the infinite bucket.'
result.scope_notes: The diff was not provided in the patch dump, but commit metadata indicates a small 60-line addition across 2 files including unit tests.
result.card: Validates the bucket array read from the fee estimates data file upon startup. A corrupted or malformed fee estimates file lacking an infinite final bucket causes feerate lookups to read past the end of the bucket map. The change rejects estimate files where buckets are non-positive, not strictly increasing, or not terminated with an infinite bucket, adding unit tests for each malformed case.

risk.why: A flaw in bucket validation could cause a node to reject a valid fee estimates file on startup, forcing fee estimates to rebuild from scratch.
